text:
Owen Phillips: heads up: we have a Dedicated customer escalation (Enterprise) asking for written latency/availability expectations + what we do when things degrade. They’re referencing “Dedicated should have better SLO than Hosted” and want something we can send this week. This is off SUP-3950. Any guidance / draft language we can use?

Dev Patel: :eyes: can you paste the exact ask / what they’re seeing (region, model, time window)? Also want to make sure we don’t promise contract terms.

Owen Phillips: customer ask verbatim: “Can you document expected uptime and p99 latency for our dedicated pool, and what happens if those aren’t met (failover, throttling, status updates)? We’re seeing intermittent 5xx and spikes to multi-second TTFT.”
Context: us-east-1, Dedicated pool pinned to `rwi-llama-70b` (their name for it), last ~2 weeks. They mention a couple of brief brownouts and 2 incidents where streaming disconnected mid-response.

Rachel Kim: this is the same account that asked for “SLOs + operational behavior” in renewal prep. We should align with the tiered SLO publication so we don’t send one-off numbers that change next week.

Lauren Bishop: yep. We should anchor on the tier principles + the draft Dedicated SLO table (but frame as “targets / program” unless it’s already in their contract). Dedicated messaging:
- reserved capacity + isolation
- more predictable throughput/latency vs Hosted, but still subject to model/runtime behavior and upstream dependencies
- incident comms path is tighter (dedicated-oncall + named escalation)
I can share the short internal blurb we’ve been using while SRE finalizes numbers.

Sean Gallagher: we’re ~final on the tiered SLO definitions doc; publishing internally now, external/customer-facing version coming after review.
For Support: please avoid quoting a single p99 number without the context (route + streaming vs non-streaming + TTFT vs full duration). The doc splits those.
If helpful, you can reference:
- Availability SLI = successful responses / total valid requests (excludes invalid auth, malformed, customer aborts)
- Streaming has separate SLIs: time-to-first-token and disconnect rate
- Dedicated adds “pool readiness” (capacity signal) but that’s not a customer-facing KPI yet.

Rafael Mendes: +1. For this week, I’d suggest:
1) confirm we’re rolling out tiered SLOs and will share the formal doc once published
2) provide “current operating targets” at a high level (e.g., monthly availability target for Dedicated, and that latency targets are per-route and measured at p95/p99)
3) explicitly state what we do operationally: mitigation hierarchy (rollback → routing adjustments within their pool → controlled failover if configured)
We can also loop in SRE on their specific metrics to see if they’re burning budget vs just isolated spikes.

Aisha Bello: here’s the internal Confluence draft link (not customer-shareable yet): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Tiered+SLO+definitions+-+Hosted+vs+Dedicated
If you need a snippet, use this sanitized framing:
- Dedicated: target availability measured over a rolling 30d window, scoped to the customer’s dedicated endpoints in a region.
- Latency: measured separately for (a) non-streaming request latency and (b) streaming TTFT; we track p95/p99.
- Disconnects: we classify client abort vs server disconnect; only server-side disconnects count against us.
- Exclusions: customer-side timeouts, client-initiated disconnects, invalid requests/auth.

Nikhil Sharma: also worth clarifying model pinning: if they’re pinned to a specific model build, we won’t silently swap them unless they opt into fallback. That’s a Dedicated difference vs Hosted.

Dev Patel: can we give Support a “safe” paragraph? Something like:
“Dedicated is designed for higher predictability and isolation. We operate against tier-specific reliability targets (availability + latency SLIs) and actively mitigate incidents via rollback and controlled routing adjustments. We’ll share the finalized SLO document once published; meanwhile we can review your pool’s last-14d performance and proposed mitigations.”

Lauren Bishop: I’ll draft a customer-facing note and paste here for review.

Lauren Bishop: draft (Support can use, pls tweak as needed):
“Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU capacity with tenant isolation and is operated against Dedicated-tier reliability targets (availability and latency SLIs). We measure latency separately for streaming and non-streaming endpoints (including time-to-first-token for streaming) and track both p95 and p99. During incidents, our oncall team prioritizes restoring service via rollback and targeted mitigations within your dedicated pool; any failover/fallback behavior is controlled and will only be enabled if configured for your deployment. We’re in the process of publishing the formal tiered SLO definitions and error budget policy; we can share the finalized document as soon as it’s approved. In parallel, we’re reviewing your recent 5xx/latency spikes by region/model to identify the root cause and immediate mitigations.”

Sean Gallagher: looks good. Two tweaks:
- remove “error budget policy” from customer-facing phrasing unless we’re sure they’re ready for it (some customers interpret it as us “allowing downtime”). Maybe say “reliability policy” or “operational program.”
- add a line about comms: status page + direct escalation path for Dedicated.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also ask Support to capture specific timestamps + request IDs so we can correlate with the streaming disconnect classification (some of those are 499 client aborts).

Owen Phillips: super helpful. I’ll send the edited note + request IDs. Rachel — do you want to be included on the customer email thread?

Rachel Kim: yes pls. Also flag if they ask for “credits” — that’s a separate path, but we should be consistent with what’s in their MSA.

Aisha Bello: if you paste a couple request IDs here (or in a private thread), I can sanity check whether the disconnects were client abort vs server-side. We had a known classification gap we’re closing.

Owen Phillips: will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
